record.original_question: Nelson--Nguyen conjecture: Subspace embedding properties of sparse random matrices: Prove or disprove the Nelson--Nguyen conjecture: A SparseStack embedding with parameters $ = O(( r) / epsilon)$ and $k = O(r / epsilon^2)$ is an oblivious subspace embedding with parameters $alpha = 1 - epsilon$ and $beta = 1+epsilon$.

evidence.quote: Prove or disprove the Nelson--Nguyen conjecture: A SparseStack embedding with parameters $\zeta = \mathcal{O}((\log r) / \varepsilon)$ and $k = \mathcal{O}(r / \varepsilon^2)$ is an oblivious subspace embedding with parameters $\alpha = 1 - \varepsilon$ and $\beta = 1+\varepsilon$.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. For integers $n \geq m \geq 1$, an $m \times n$ random matrix $S$ is called an oblivious subspace embedding (OSE) with parameters $(\alpha, \beta)$, distortion, and rank $r$, if for every fixed $r$-dimensional linear subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, with high probability one has
$$\alpha \, \|x\|_2 \;\leq\; \|S x\|_2 \;\leq\; \beta \, \|x\|_2 \qquad \text{for all } x \in V.$$

The SparseStack construction with parameters $(k, \zeta)$, where $k$ is the number of rows and $\zeta$ is the column sparsity, is the random $k \times n$ matrix obtained as follows. Partition the $k$ rows into $\zeta$ equal blocks of size $k/\zeta$. In each block, every column is zero except in one row chosen independently and uniformly at random, where the entry is an independent $\pm 1/\sqrt{\zeta}$ Rademacher random variable. The full SparseStack matrix is the vertical stack of these $\zeta$ independent block matrices.

Problem (Nelson–Nguyen conjecture). Let $r \geq 1$ be an integer and $\varepsilon \in (0, 1)$. Prove or disprove: there exist absolute constants such that the SparseStack embedding with column sparsity 
$$\zeta = O\!\left(\frac{\log r}{\varepsilon}\right) \quad\text{and number of rows}\quad k = O\!\left(\frac{r}{\varepsilon^2}\right)$$
is an oblivious subspace embedding for $r$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with parameters $\alpha = 1 - \varepsilon$ and $\beta = 1 + \varepsilon$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Nelson–Nguyen conjecture has seen substantial recent progress but is not fully resolved at the exact target parameters. Chenakkod, Dereziński, Dong, and Rudelson (arXiv:2311.10680, 2023) established optimal embedding dimension m = O(d/ε²) with sparsity O(log⁴ d) per column. Dereziński, Yang and collaborators (arXiv:2411.08773, 2024) achieved optimal dimension with near-optimal sparsity Õ(1/ε). A 2025 work (arXiv:2508.14234) is titled "Resolving Nelson–Nguyen Conjecture Up to Sub-Polylogarithmic Factors," indicating the conjecture is settled up to sub-polylogarithmic factors but not at the precise O((log r)/ε), O(r/ε²) bounds.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Embedding Dimension for Sparse Subspace Embeddings
status_evidence.snippet: random matrix with m ≥ (1+θ)d dimensions … with s = O(log^4 d) non-zeros per column is an OSE
status_evidence.claim: Optimal embedding dimension achieved with polylogarithmic, not logarithmic, sparsity.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Oblivious Subspace Embeddings with Near-optimal Sparsity
status_evidence.snippet: optimal dimension m=Θ(d/ε²) with near-optimal sparsity Õ(1/ε) per column
status_evidence.claim: Near-optimal sparsity achieved, nearly matching the Nelson–Nguyen conjecture.
